description.narrative: The IDF Grant will contribute to improving governance and business climate in the Republic of Tajikistan through creating capacity for tax service reforms. In the last ten years there has been virtually no improvement in the Tajik tax service. Tax to GDP ratio remains among the lowest among CIS countries (16.8 including social payments). Tax arrears have risen by about 65 million somoni in 2006 alonecomma and stand at 224 million somoni. representing more than 20 percent of net annual collection. Business processes of Tajik tax service are manualcomma inefficientcomma and lack transparency. Perhaps most importantlycomma despite commitment of the highest leadershipcomma there is a lack of capacity on all levels to implement reforms. The tax system is incapable to sustain further increase in the collection of revenue without a comprehensive reform that would increase capacitycomma introduce modern and transparent business practicescomma and ensure voluntary compliance of the majority of tax payers. The above reforms would have far-reaching implications for improved governance and business climate in the countrycomma supporting further growth and development. In particularcomma this grant will support TC in the following areas: (i) developing a comprehensive strategy for tax reformscomma including conducting a functional reviewcomma IT review and a thorough analysis of institutional development needscomma and development of a concept paper for comprehensive tax modernization; (ii) supporting implementation of urgent reformscomma such as adoption of taxpayer register; harmonization of the Tax Code with the Civil Code; and (iii) strengthening human capital and institutional capacity of TCcomma including training in collection of tax arrearscomma and collection of social security taxescomma as well as capacity building in the TC to implement and manage reforms. The authorities of the Republic of Tajikistan are committed to modernizing their tax system. This Grant proposal responds to an urgent request for assistance by the Chairman of TC. Howevercomma besides the leadership of the Tax Committeecomma the team has discussed these issues with the high-level policy decision-makers such as the Economic Advisor to the President and the Minister of Financecomma who fully support the modernization of the tax system. The request for assistance is formulated both in terms of the immediate needs of the Tax Committee and medium-term comprehensive tax modernization effort. While the IDF grant would lay the groundwork for tax system modernization by supporting the strategy developmentcomma urgent reformscomma and capacity buildingcomma the mid- to long-term reform needs of TC could possibly be addressed by securing a multi-donor trust fund at a future date.
